claims: Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026, at 6:35 p.m. EDT from Launch Complex 39B at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
Artemis II began a 10-day crewed mission around the Moon.
The Orion spacecraft carried four astronauts.
The Orion spacecraft is currently on a trajectory to the Moon.
Artemis II marks the first crewed return to the lunar vicinity in over 50 years.
The Artemis II crew has completed initial orbital maneuvers.
The Artemis II crew is transitioning to a lunar trajectory.
Artemis II is crewed by Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The goal of Artemis II is to test systems for future moon landings.
The Artemis II launch was visible from large parts of Florida and southern Georgia.
The Orion capsule will return and land in the Pacific Ocean after looping around the Moon.
